- Leaving board to practice law.
- Laura Monick will be taking over as Ohio delegate.

Will discuss Rules Drafts if/when commission has reached Quorum.

Finance- Meets next week, March 19, 2025 3 p.m. ET.

Communications- Working on a welcome letter and one pager. Then will work through other documents on the PA Compact website. Meets next April 14, 2025 12 p.m. ET.

Next Steps Discussion about next steps for the Data System: There will not be a rules hearing at the full commission meeting April 25. Instead, commission can invite these groups to present and work towards developing an RFP.

- Invite groups to demo their system

## Rule 2 Draft

Chair Terranova gives background of PA Compact development and drafting team.

- Regulator concerns are understood but it is commission's job to implement law as it is written.
- Focus this discussion on if commission has the authority to implement rule 2

N. Kalfas summarizes her thoughts and concerns- does not think commission has authority for rule 2 as drafted.

- Believes the choice of a qualifying license as opposed to a home state license was deliberate, after hearing from a rules committee member that was involved in the drafting and reviewing the memo from the drafting attorneys
- o Memo from drafting attorneys - explained different types of compact models and guided PA drafting team
- From a plain text read, the definitions are explicit
- Qualifying license is that entry into the compact, the definition does not direct rulemaking authority
- Section 5 of compact does grant rulemaking authority but then lists process requirements. This conflicts.

S. Loucka summarizes what rules committee has been working on

- The rules committee drafted rule 2 without the guidance that they should not further qualify the qualifying license
- Believes that most of the rules committee and most of the commission would vote to pass rule 2 as drafted, however the question is does the commission have that authority
- J. Alley asks N. Kalfas for her official legal opinion.
- N. Kalfas - With the addition of memo and the rules committee member's statement, it would not be appropriate for committee to move forward with a rule that further defines qualifying license. No I do not think the commission has authority.
- J. Alley asks about legislative intent.
- N. Kalfas - we don't have a lot of information about state intent.
- T. Terranova adds that he does agree that the way it is written does not allow for further qualifiers and spoke to his legislature about this when the bill was introduced, they adopted it anyway.
- L. Marx suggest sending the draft back to Rules Committee without all the qualifications but still with some elements wanted from applicants.
